feedback.problem: What is the coefficient of $(x-2)^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)={e}^{-{x}^{2}}$ at $x=2?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=2$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2)+\frac{{f}^{″}(2)}{2}(x-2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $(x-2)^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is

$$
\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(2).
$$

$$

$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{-{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-2x{e}^{-{x}^{2}} \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-2{e}^{-{x}^{2}}+4{x}^{2}{e}^{-{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(2) & =-2{e}^{-{2}^{2}}+4\cdot {2}^{2}\cdot {e}^{-{2}^{2}} \\  & =-2{e}^{-4}+16{e}^{-4} \\  & =14{e}^{-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x-2)^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(2)}{2} & =\frac{14{e}^{-4}}{2}=7{e}^{-4}\end{aligned}
$$
